title: Two Actions from One State: Fork Futures Teach JEPA World Models to Compare
abstract: arXiv:2611.28350v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: JEPA world models are trained to predict logged transitions but used to compare counterfactual actions from one state. The logged behavior data show one action per state, and under a local linear approximation we prove the action response is unidentified along any direction the policy never varies within a state. We therefore supplement behavior data with measured outcomes of alternative actions from the same state. Our fork futures execute two actions from one restored state, and their outcome difference cancels the state term, identifying the action response on the sampled span. The resulting model, Fork-JEPA, matches predicted to measured differences, anchors the logged successor with behavior prediction, and adds a lookback head that keeps the predecessor recoverable, all at training time, leaving planning unchanged. On three visual control tasks, behavior-only training leaves the predicted action effect no better than a constant g

translated_title: 一状态双动作：分叉未来教会JEPA世界模型进行比较
translated_abstract: JEPA世界模型的训练目标是预测记录的状态转移，但在实际使用时却需要从单一状态比较反事实动作。行为日志数据中每个状态只包含一个动作，并且在局部线性近似下，我们证明了在策略从未发生变化的方向上，动作响应是不可辨识的。因此，我们用来自同一状态的替代动作的实测结果来补充行为数据。我们的“分叉未来”方法从同一恢复状态执行两个动作，其结果差异消去了状态项，从而在采样范围内辨识出动作响应。由此得到的模型Fork-JEPA将预测差异与实测差异相匹配，用行为预测锚定记录的后继状态，并添加一个回看头以保持前驱状态可恢复——所有这些修改都在训练时完成，规划过程保持不变。在三个视觉控制任务上，仅用行为数据训练会使预测的动作效果不优于一个常数
tldr: 提出Fork-JEPA，通过从同一恢复状态执行两个动作并利用其实测结果差异消去状态项，解决了仅用行为数据训练JEPA世界模型时动作响应不可辨识的问题。
en_tdlr: Fork-JEPA addresses the unidentifiability of action responses in JEPA world models trained on behavior-only data by executing two actions from one restored state, using their measured outcome difference to cancel the state term.
